original_question: Let X be a compact Kahler manifold, let alpha_0 be a Kahler class, and let S_0 be a positive closed current representing alpha_0 with possibly nonzero Lelong numbers. Di Nezza and Lu construct a maximal weak Kahler-Ricci flow (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} that is smooth on time-increasing Zariski open sets. Determine whether this flow produces approximants with analytic singularities.
target_in_paper: Question 43 (DiNezza-Lu) in §6.4.1: "Does the Kähler-Ricci flow produce approximants with analytic singularities ?" ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Globally the objects constructed by DiNezza and Lu are positive currents; only on a time-increasing family of Zariski open subsets Omega_t are they honest Kähler forms satisfying the Kähler–Ricci flow equation. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, 'approximants' should be identified explicitly with the currents omega_t for t > 0 that approach S_0 as t decreases to 0. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The phrase 'analytic singularities' should be defined using Definition 3.4: locally a potential u of the current has the form u = (c/2) log(sum_j |f_j|^2) + v, where c > 0, v is smooth, and the f_j are holomorphic. The sharp paper-faithful quantifier is whether each flowing current omega_t has analytic singularities, i.e. whether the Kähler–Ricci flow itself yields analytic-singularity approximants of S_0. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold, let alpha_0 in H^{1,1}(X, R) be a Kähler cohomology class, and let S_0 be a positive closed (1,1)-current representing alpha_0. Consider the Kähler–Ricci flow starting at S_0, namely a family (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} satisfying d/dt omega_t = -Ric(omega_t), omega_t -> S_0 weakly as t -> 0, and T_max = sup{ t >= 0 | t K_X + alpha_0 is Kähler }. When S_0 has some nonzero Lelong numbers, DiNezza and Lu construct a maximal family of positive currents (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} that are honest Kähler forms on time-increasing Zariski open subsets Omega_t where they satisfy the flow equation. Is it true that, for every t in (0, T_max), the current omega_t has analytic singularities in the sense that its local potentials are of the form (c/2) log(sum_j |f_j|^2) + v with c > 0, v smooth, and the f_j holomorphic; equivalently, does the Kähler–Ricci flow itself provide analytic-singularity approximants of S_0 as t -> 0^+? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at any front-of-paper conjecture or theorem; it matches the later open problem in §6.4.1 almost verbatim. In that subsection the authors fix exactly the data you mention (compact Kähler X, Kähler class alpha_0, positive closed current S_0), define the Kähler–Ricci flow starting at S_0 and the maximal time T_max, recall the DiNezza–Lu results for zero versus nonzero Lelong numbers, and then ask Question 43: whether the flow produces approximants with analytic singularities. To make this into a sharp stand-alone research question, one must import the earlier formal definition of analytic singularities from Definition 3.4. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
